candidate.title: PIP-Seq
candidate.scope: Protein interaction profile sequencing (PIP-seq), at the level of the assigned Illumina schematic: formaldehyde-crosslinked RNA-protein starting material, cell lysis/DNase, and four separate dsRNase/ssRNase footprint and protein-depleted control routes through RNA recovery, size selection, normalization and strand-specific sequencing. The expanded name and capitalization variants denote the same target. The leftmost assay-name icon is descriptive, not an extra chemical transformation. UV and noncrosslinked preparations mentioned in catalogue prose, plant nuclear applications, and associated kit names do not add targets to this drawing. The diagram compresses the library/DSN interface; explicit corrections place library construction before library-directed DSN while retaining each drawn branch and its terminal sequencing destination. This is a schematic architecture, not an execution protocol.

method_scopes.rationale: All four drawn routes belong to PIP-seq: dsRNase footprint, dsRNase protein-depleted control, ssRNase footprint and ssRNase protein-depleted control. The target label is an alias of Protein Interaction Profile Sequencing, not a second method. The fixed formaldehyde starting history applies throughout this local graph; UV and no-crosslink variants in surrounding prose are not assigned to these fixed input states. Shared captions are expanded into branch-specific local operations, with no pooling. Library preparation and sequencing are two components of the single combined terminal caption, separated only to resolve the primary-supported DSN interface explicitly. RNA sequence/strand and matched footprint-versus-control enrichment support protein-protected-site interpretation, rather than identifying a particular RBP. Formaldehyde can preserve protein-protein contacts and merge nearby binding events, so neither survival nor an extended protected region establishes a single direct protein contact. No historical development, interchangeability, or unshown analysis workflow is asserted.
